summary.title: PerceptionRubrics: Calibrating Multimodal Evaluation to Human Perception

details: Perception benchmarks are saturated and use linear/holistic similarity scoring that dilutes fatal localized errors, so high scores mask real perceptual brittleness and misalign with human sensitivity.

PerceptionRubrics: 1,038 information-dense images paired with >10,000 instance-specific atomic rubrics, split into 'Must-Right' (essential visual facts) and 'Easy-Wrong' (error-prone details mined from actual model errors) streams.
Gated scoring metric: failing any single Must-Right rubric zeroes the score; otherwise score is the pass fraction over Easy-Wrong rubrics, making the metric non-linear like human verification.

Caption-centric pipeline to avoid the image-to-rubric grounding gap: 'golden captions' are first synthesized via a Circular Peer-Review consensus among heterogeneous frontier MLLMs (compare/rank/rewrite, discard-on-divergence, lightweight human verification), then distilled into atomic verifiable rubrics.
Seven domains: Natural Scenes, Document & OCR, Digital UI/UX, Structured Data (charts/tables), STEM & Expert, Logic & Puzzle, Creative & Cultural; images sourced from open visual benchmarks.
Density-aware filtering with Step3-VL-10B scoring visual complexity and informativeness (1-10) with domain-specific thresholds.
Statistics: 1,038 images/captions, mean golden caption 770.42 words (median 569, tail to 3,461), 10,718 rubrics (4,053 Must-Right, 6,665 Easy-Wrong), 10.33 rubrics/image.
Golden-caption jury/generators: GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Seed-1.8 (<=2 peer-review iterations).
Rubric proposer: Gemini-3-Pro with domain-adaptive prompts; Easy-Wrong rubrics derived by contrasting a pool of ~8 baseline MLLM responses against the golden caption.
Judge: GPT-OSS-120B outputting boolean per rubric (GPT-5.5 used as alternate judge).

25 MLLMs: proprietary (Gemini-3/3.1-Pro, Gemini-3/3.5-Flash, GPT-5.4/5.5, GPT-4o, Seed-1.6/1.8/2.0-Pro/2.0-Lite, GLM-5V-Turbo, Qwen3.5/3.6-Plus) and open-weight (Qwen2.5-VL 7B/32B, Qwen3-VL 8B/235B-A22B, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, Step3-VL-10B, Step-3.7-Flash, MiniMax-M3, MiMo-V2.5, Kimi-K2.5/K2.6).
Human alignment: correlation of benchmark scores with Vision Arena Elo on five overlapping models, compared against DOCCI and DetailCaps.
Length-bias check (score vs. response word count), judge-swap robustness, and rubric subsampling at 20/40/60/80% with three runs each to measure score standard deviation.
Reported diagnostics: Must-Right item accuracy, Easy-Wrong item accuracy, gate pass rate (all Must-Right correct), per-domain breakdown, failure-source distribution.

key_findings.finding: There is a large 'Reliability Gap': models pass individual atomic rubrics at high rates but often fail the strict conjunction of all mandatory facts.
key_findings.evidence: Must-Right item accuracy is far above the sample-level gate pass rate for weaker models (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-7B 64.99% item vs 26.20% gate; Qwen2.5-VL-32B 76.30% vs 39.40%), and the gap narrows for stronger models (Gemini-3.1-Pro 95.69% vs 84.49%).

key_findings.finding: A persistent ~8% perception deficit separates the open-source frontier from proprietary leaders, unlike the near-convergence seen in reasoning tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Best open model Qwen3.5-397B-A17B scores 61.61% overall vs Seed-2.0-Lite 70.07% and Gemini-3.5-Flash 69.88%; GPT-4o-2024-05-13 is the weakest proprietary at 12.59%.

key_findings.finding: PerceptionRubrics aligns with human preference far better than existing captioning benchmarks.
key_findings.evidence: Against Vision Arena Elo over five shared models, PerceptionRubrics attains Pearson 0.916 and Spearman 1.000, while DOCCI assigns nearly indistinguishable scores to models with markedly different Elo, and DetailCaps also correlates weakly.

key_findings.finding: Information-dense, spatially constrained GUI inputs are the dominant failure mode, while natural scenes are comparatively mature.
key_findings.evidence: Almost all models score lowest on GUI (Qwen2.5-VL-7B 5.13%, Seed-2.0-Lite 59.07%) versus highest on Natural (Seed-2.0-Lite 79.20%), and GUI is the largest source of Must-Right gate failures across six representative models.

key_findings.finding: Fine-grained hallucination resistance is almost fully determined by foundational perceptual reliability.
key_findings.evidence: Must-Right pass rate and Easy-Wrong accuracy across six representative models show near-perfect linear correlation (R^2 ≈ 0.98).
